Therapeutic

thair-uh-PYOO-tik -- stress on the third syllable, PYOO. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Therapeutic is healing or corrective; helping to restore health or well-being.

The hospital offers therapeutic music sessions that ease patients' pain and lower their stress.

Worked Example

After the wildfire, counselors set up daily art sessions where children paint what they saw, and week by week the drawings -- and the children -- grow calmer.

The art sessions are therapeutic: they actively help the children heal. Therapeutic covers whatever restores health or well-being, whether the healing is physical, emotional, or both.

How Therapeutic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

healing

healing: restoring health or soundness

restorative

restorative: giving back strength or well-being

curative

curative: able to cure a disease or condition

Antonyms

harmful

harmful: causing damage or injury

injurious

injurious: causing harm, especially to health

How Strong Is It? — restorative → curative → therapeutic

restorative vs. therapeutic

restorative vs. therapeutic: Restorative is the gentler claim -- a restorative nap gives back energy, while calling something therapeutic suggests it genuinely helps heal a real hurt, whether in the body or the mind.

curative vs. therapeutic

curative vs. therapeutic: Curative makes a stronger promise than therapeutic: a therapeutic treatment helps you heal and feel better, while a curative one claims to eliminate the illness itself, start to finish.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — therap-

root — therap-: to treat medically, take care of, serve (Greek therapeuein)

suffix — -ic

suffix — -ic: having the characteristics of; like (Greek -ikos, via Latin -icus)

Put it together

Put it together: Therapeutic builds on Greek therapeuein, 'to treat medically, to take care of.' Something therapeutic has the character of treatment and care -- it works to heal, correct, and restore, the same root that gives us therapy itself.

Use the root in a new word: therapist

Use the root in a new word: therapist: After the accident, a physical therapist helped him regain full movement in his knee.

Root Check

Word Choice

Therapeutic works at two volumes: the strict medical sense (a therapeutic dose, therapeutic exercises) and the everyday sense for anything that soothes and restores ('I find folding laundry oddly therapeutic'). Both flow from the same idea -- treatment and care that heal.
